coverage.backend_cluster_note: InfoTracer and SearchQuarry use a similar form stack and browser challenge. Drift on one should trigger a review of both.

false_success_traps: If the page still asks you to enter your information, pick a state, and enter a city, nothing was sent.
Search results on this site are a partly hidden preview behind a paywall. A later check there gives weak proof either way.
The optional receipt email can fail with a message that the robot check is not valid. This project treats the removal as accepted in that case, but there is then no email receipt.
The page that says it is checking whether your data is available is a loading page, not a result.
The site's name search now hands off to another company's host. It is not confirmed that SearchQuarry still shows its own results page, so a later check may not be able to prove removal.
genuine_confirmation: After you tick your records and press remove, the page speaks about confirmation of your opt-out request and offers to email it to you. The page no longer shows the first form asking for name, state, and city.
name: SearchQuarry

opt_out_url_check.note: HTTP 200. The page title is the SearchQuarry data removal process. The form itself was not seen in a plain page request.

steps: Open the SearchQuarry data removal page.
Pass the robot check if one appears.
Wait while the page says it is checking whether your data is available. The form shows after that.
On the opt-out form, fill in the first name and last name. Pick the state and fill in the city shown on the listing.
Pass the robot check again if it appears, then submit. Another robot check may follow.
The page lists matching records. Tick the ones that are yours and press the remove button.
The page then offers to email a confirmation of the opt-out request. Enter an email address and send it if you want that receipt. The receipt is optional.
